correctness.rationale: Every finite-welfare coalition is connected and every nontrivial connected coalition contains a hub. Separated hubs force two full stars; joined hubs admit only (p,q)=(a,0),(0,b),(1,1) by independent leaf entry/exit inequalities, with hub deviations never profitable. Thus exactly \(ab+3\) Nash partitions. Pairwise distance scores give \(W(p,q)=2(1+p+q-pq)\), capped by \(2(a+b)\), and the worst Nash welfare is four. Standard-library exhaustive checking directly enumerated 217,219 labeled partitions across 18 parameter pairs; infinite result established by proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Two-hub trees provide the simplest natural topology where distance 1, 2 and 3 contributions all occur. The all-size equilibrium partition classification, exact labeled count and complete welfare spectrum quantify the gap between efficient Nash existence and worst-case Nash selection: \(\mathrm{PoS}=1\) but \(\mathrm{PoA}=(a+b)/2\), linear despite uniformly bounded diameter and treewidth. This is not a simple graph renaming, textbook consequence, or result implied by the known general optimization algorithms.
